maya: Heads-up — we're seeing a late-data spike for EU ingestion window 04:00-06:00 UTC. A bunch of hourly aggregates are still stale. I want to avoid a full cluster backfill if possible. Thoughts? :eyes:

jon: How big is the spike? Are we missing raw events or just delayed commits from the shard leader? Can you paste the anomaly query?

maya: Quick shape: +2.3M events queued, mostly tenant prefixes eu-*. Latency tail for kafka->ingest is ~12m for those partitions. Query I ran:```sql
SELECT shard, count(*) AS pending FROM ingest.buffer WHERE tenant LIKE 'eu-%' AND received_at BETWEEN '2026-03-21T04:00:00Z' AND '2026-03-21T06:00:00Z' GROUP BY shard ORDER BY pending DESC LIMIT 10;```

sam: If it's partitioned to a few hot shards we can do a targeted "catch-up" run for those shards instead of a full replay. Use small concurrency and prefix KV-cache warmup to avoid SLO hits. e.g.:
```bash
catchup-runner --shard sh-23,sh-45 --window 04:00-06:00 --mode targeted --concurrency 4 --kv-warmup=on
```
Set a global rate cap via the console so it doesn't steal slots from normal ingest.

lee: FWIW, console quotas don't currently expose a temporary "operator-burst" lane. If we run catchup under normal quota it will be fair-shared and could take ages. We can cheat: spin the job with tag `priority: rescue` and use the operator token which gets elevated capacity (short-lived). Ops + SRE need to approve.

jon: We should also avoid regenerating upstream aggregates if the cached prefix exists. Suggest flow: 1) replay raw events -> 2) append-only delta aggregates -> 3) run aggregate-merge for affected hourly buckets. That minimizes downstream churn.

maya: Good point. Can we disable full-merge for now and only run merge for hours that show delta > threshold?

sam: Yes. The CLI supports `--delta-threshold`. e.g. `--delta-threshold 0.02` to only merge buckets with >2% change. Also recommend `--dry-run` first to estimate token/quota usage:```bash
catchup-runner --shard sh-23 --window 04:00-06:00 --mode targeted --dry-run --output-estimate
```

telemetry-bot: [alert] Late-data spike detected for tenant-prefix eu-* at 2026-03-21T06:12:34Z. Linked incident: #INC-2026-331.

lee: Ops: if you want the operator token flow I can open an approval in the console (will require 2 approvals). Otherwise we throttle via `--qps 50`. Also add `--route avoid:production-critical` to keep routing away from our low-latency tier.

maya: Ok let's do a targeted run for top 3 shards (sh-23 sh-45 sh-11) with conservative qps and delta-threshold. @jon can you own the run? @lee please start the approval if we need operator token. We plan start at 18:30 UTC.

jon: I can take it. Plan:
- dry-run now to get estimates
- if estimate < 10% of daily quota, proceed with operator token bypass. else proceed with throttled run.
Commands I will run:```bash
# estimate
catchup-runner --shard sh-23,sh-45,sh-11 --window 04:00-06:00 --mode targeted --dry-run --output-estimate
# actual (if approved)
catchup-runner --shard sh-23,sh-45,sh-11 --window 04:00-06:00 --mode targeted --concurrency 4 --qps 50 --delta-threshold 0.02 --route avoid:production-critical --tag priority:rescue --operator-token $OP_TOKEN
```

maya: Cool. Put a note in the runbook with the exact command and a rollback trigger: if error rate on ingest-slo > 0.5% for 5m abort.

jon: Doable. I'll paste initial dry-run numbers in ~10m.

telemetry-bot: [info] Dry-run estimate: expected events to replay 1.8M, projected console quota consumption ~7.4% of daily EU token budget.

maya: Sounds safe. Lee — still need approvals?

lee: Approval requested. Added approvers: @sam, @maya. ETA for approvals: ~2min.

sam: Approved. :thumbsup:

maya: Approved. kicking off at 18:30 UTC (manual start). tagging incident thread #INC-2026-331 for visibility.

jon: Starting actual run now (operator token used). Monitoring dashboards: https://console.internal/redwood/telemetry/dashboards/late-data-eu (watching ingest-slo and aggregate-delays).

jon: Quick log snippet:```
[18:31:05] catchup-runner: shard=sh-23 replayed=420k elapsed=2m qps=48 errors=0
[18:33:10] catchup-runner: shard=sh-45 replayed=720k elapsed=4m qps=50 errors=1
```

maya: Nice. Keeping an eye on downstream aggregate merges. If we see >0.2% variance, pause and run narrower merge.

tea: small note: please post the final summary (counts, quota used, any regressions) back to the incident thread so product can close the ticket.

jon: Will do. So far no SLO uptick. I'll post summary in ~20m. :white_check_mark:
